title: Delivery & Pickup Appointments Terms: Rescheduling a Booked Appointment
content:
A customer may move a booked Delivery & Pickup Appointment to another date or window, on the terms below.

## Terms

**1. Status.** An appointment is rescheduled only while its status is scheduled. The status is read from the system record of that appointment.

**2. Notice.** A reschedule is requested no later than the fulfillment method's reschedule notice hours before the start of the booked window. Notice hours are counted backwards in full elapsed hours from the window start time on the scheduled date, in the delivery address's local time. A request made exactly the notice hours before the window start is in time.

**3. Requests inside the notice period.** A request made inside the notice period is not a reschedule. The customer either keeps the appointment, or, when nobody is present, the appointment is treated as a customer-caused miss.

**4. Free and charged reschedules.** The method's free reschedules carry no charge. Each customer reschedule after those bills the method's reschedule fee as its own fee entry for the new appointment date.

**5. Maximum.** No reschedule is accepted once the appointment's reschedule count has reached the method's maximum total reschedules.

**6. Severe weather.** When the method's weather switch is on, a reschedule forced by a severe-weather advisory for the delivery area is free and is not counted. The reschedule count does not increase.

**7. Moves made by Kestrel.** A move made by Kestrel is never a customer reschedule.

**8. The new date.** The new date must meet the same rules as a booking: the minimum lead days, the maximum horizon days, the method's appointment days, its holiday closures and its windows.

## Notice: boundary cases (hypothetical 24-hour notice, window 12:00-16:00 on the scheduled date, times in the delivery address's local time)

| Request made | Full elapsed hours before the 12:00 window start | Reschedule? |
|---|---|---|
| 11:00 the day before | 25 | Yes, in time |
| 12:00 the day before | 24 | Yes, in time (the boundary itself) |
| 12:30 the day before | 23 (23 hours 30 minutes is not 24 full hours) | No, inside the notice period |
| 09:00 on the scheduled date | 3 | No, inside the notice period |

## Count and fee: hypothetical method with 2 free reschedules, a $40.00 fee and a maximum of 4

| Customer reschedule | Reschedule count before the request | Accepted? | Fee billed |
|---|---|---|---|
| First | 0 | Yes | none |
| Second | 1 | Yes | none |
| Third | 2 | Yes | $40.00, for the new appointment date |
| Fourth | 3 | Yes | $40.00, for the new appointment date |
| Fifth | 4 | No: the count has reached the maximum | none |

If one of these moves had been forced by a severe-weather advisory, with the weather switch on, that move would be free. It would leave the count where it was, so the free and maximum figures would apply as though the move had not happened.

## Basis questions

**Kestrel moved the appointment. Does that use up one of the customer's free reschedules?** No. A move made by Kestrel is never a customer reschedule.

**Can a dispatched appointment be rescheduled?** No. Rescheduling is open only while the status is scheduled.
